_comment: Curated per-system facts, merged into generation. Keyed by (sector, hex); 'world' is checked against TravellerMap so a mistyped hex fails loudly. Validate with: cargo run --bin validate-overrides --features backend

overrides.note:
Drinaxian Companion ch.5. TravellerMap already gives F4 V, PBG 624 (2 belts, 4 gas giants) and W=16, so only the named bodies are recorded. Traefar is "the next world out from Torpol", said relatively because that is what the book says — the absolute orbit is a derived fact that would go stale if generation shifted. Its UWP is now given in full (G410466-7) rather than as the partial the book's prose supported, so every column is stated rather than rolled around the two digits that were known.

The book splits the two belts by role: "The outer planetoid belt has an extensive belter community whilst the inner one has less belters but more commercial mining operations... the Imperial megacorporation Sternmetal Horizons also has a mining base in the inner belt." Unpinned, both belts generated far out at orbits 10 and 11 (11,548 and 23,038 Mkm), which makes the inner one a month's travel from Torpol and nothing like the near-at-hand mining ground the text describes.

So the inner belt is pinned to orbit 6, the one orbit between Torpol (orbit 5) and Traefar, carrying the mining facility for Sternmetal Horizons' base and the Provost-owned claims — the Provosts being Torpol's ruling merchant council, which is what "local companies operating out of Torpol" means. Orbit 6 is 778 Mkm, not the ~600 Mkm the placement was asked for: orbit radii are a fixed Traveller grid (orbit 5 is 419 Mkm, orbit 6 is 778) and 600 is not on it, so 6 is the only orbit that sits between the two worlds at all. The outer belt keeps orbit 11 (23,038 Mkm), the belter community, far enough out to be its own world. The belt that generated at orbit 10 is gone: the PBG digit fixes the count at two, and both are now spoken for.

Neither belt is named. The generator's default, "Planetoid Belt", is also what keeps `is_belt` (`size <= 0 && name.contains("planetoid")`) true, so a belt given some other name would read as a *planet* to the post-pass and "the first planet beyond Torpol" would resolve onto it and rename it Traefar. Orbit is what distinguishes inner from outer here, not a label. Under Callisto the inner belt is placed as the first orbit beyond Torpol (beyond_main 1), which is what the book describes; the outer belt keeps its Book 6 orbit, read as a distance (23,000 Mkm), far out as the book has it.

Drinaxian Companion ch.7. Star (F9 V) and 2 gas giants match TravellerMap. Bulhai is 'the system's outer gas giant'; Bulhai Freeport sits on one of its moons, pop ~20,000 (code 4). Its UWP is now given in full as C300426-B rather than pinning the port and population and rolling the rest. That makes it a class C starport, not the class F spaceport recorded earlier on the reasoning that the book's 'may come to rival the main starport at Blue' put it below Blue's B. Size 3 and a vacuum read as the moon it is; population 4 is the ~20,000 the book gives; TL B matches Blue.

Drinaxian Companion ch.11: 'Palindrome's primary is a K7 V, an orange main sequence star.' TravellerMap has K9 V. The companion (M1 V, distant, no planetary bodies of its own) and the 2 gas giants / 3 rocky worlds both match, so only the primary's class is corrected.

Reach Adventure 8: Makergod, Library Data p.31 - full system table. Counts already match TravellerMap (PBG=404 gives 4 gas giants, W=11 the non-satellite count), so what is recorded is the names, UWPs and structure upstream has no room for. Oghma's orbit is pinned because the book puts it three orbits beyond a K5 V's habitable zone and the rules agree: at size 5 the -2 DM for being outside gives a mean atmosphere of exactly the 3 it has, and the -4 hydrographics DM is why only 40% is water and that water is frozen. The book gives the tertiary as M3 V where TravellerMap has M4 V. The table is an ordered list, so under Callisto each body keeps its place in it (nth = the Book 6 orbit + 1, empty orbits counted), companions' bodies around their own star. Oghma's orbit is also read as a distance (1.0 AU, 2.5 HD around a K5 V: the Cold zone, as the book has it).

Shadows of Sindal ch.2, 'The World of Paal': 'a type F3 V (yellow-white main sequence) star... three gas giant planets and six terrestrial (rocky) worlds, of which Paal itself is second out from the sun. There are no planetoid belts.' Star and all three counts already match TravellerMap (PBG=603, W=9), so the only new fact is Paal's position.

Shadows of Sindal ch.6: 'several mining centres in the system's two asteroid belts. These feed into a modest processing facility.' Both belts already exist upstream (PBG=824); what is added is the mining on them, which a UWP cannot carry. Identified by position because the text names neither.

Pirates of Drinax bk.1 ch.3 ("Thebus") and its Proactive Recycling Corporation entry; Shadows of Sindal corroborates TravellerMap's counts ("three gas giants, two planetoid belts and several terrestrial planets, most of which are rockballs"). Olo is "the third planet in the system, a gas giant", counting Thebus itself as the first, and the PRC's base is "in orbit of Olo", in its ring debris. Magg and Magg's Moon are a referee decision: bk.1 p.123 names "the battle of Magg's Moon" without placing it; this campaign puts it around Magg, a dead world one orbit out from Olo. Book 6 reads the bodies' orbit numbers, Callisto their order (nth).

Traveller wiki, drawing on Mike Jackson's 1986 Tlaiowaha writeup in Third Imperium 02: Pourne has exactly one moon, Baen, 3,000 km across at 400,000 km. TravellerMap already supplies A9B2887-A, F3 V, PBG 902 and W=11, so only the moon is recorded. Both of Baen's numbers are derived, not quoted: satellite orbits are counted in parent diameters, and Pourne is size 9 (14,400 km), so 400,000 km is orbit 28; size 2 is the 3,000 km diameter in Traveller terms (size 2 is 3,200 km, size 1 is 1,600). Baen attaches by parent *name* rather than orbit because Pourne's own orbit is rolled, not pinned — atmosphere B puts it outside the habitable-zone rule, which is RAW and deliberate. moons is the main world's total, so the 1 here means one moon called Baen rather than a rolled moon plus Baen.

Tide-locked by referee decision, not a citation: no published source says Hilfer is locked. It is the world the tide-lock climate model was built around, and it fits the model's dry case exactly: BA5077A-6 (thin atmosphere, hydrographics 0) around an M6 V. Nothing locks a world automatically; this entry is the only reason Hilfer's map is drawn as locked. The substellar point is left to the map seed. No distance is stated: an earlier 11.1 Mkm came from Book 6's habitable zone for an M6 V, which Callisto replaces; Callisto places Hilfer by its Table 10 band.
